components.css: .ds-search { display: flex; min-height: 42px; align-items: center; gap: 9px; padding: 0 11px; border: 1px solid #fff; border-radius: 13px; background: rgb(255 255 255 / 62%); color: #172a27; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgb(29 54 49 / 4%); } .ds-search svg { width: 17px; height: 17px; flex: none; fill: none; stroke: #5b6b66; stroke-width: 1.8; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-search input { min-width: 0; border: 0; outline: 0; background: transparent; color: #172a27; font: 400 12px/1.5 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-search input::placeholder { color: #65736f; opacity: 1; } .ds-search:focus-within { border-color: rgb(23 63 58 / 25%); background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(23 63 58 / 8%); } .ds-search:focus-within input:focus-visible { outline: 0; }

narrative.overview: Groundwork uses clear frosted surfaces to keep civic tools readable over a living map. Cool city fields and deep pine controls make the interface feel calm and precise; report-state colors carry urgent meaning. Glass is structural: it separates search, navigation, and report details from the map beneath them. The Community view gives residents a familiar social reading pattern with voting, sort controls, discussion counts, and contributor context. Its cards stay crisp rather than blurred so status, source, place, and time remain easy to scan.
keyCharacteristics: The map is the primary surface; Community is a distinct second view.
Translucent glass groups controls and selected-report context over geography.
Deep pine anchors actions; status colors are semantic and always paired with labels.
Community posts use a clear vote rail and compact civic metadata.

rules.name: The Status Is Text Rule
rules.body: A status color always appears with its written status; color never carries report meaning alone.

rules.name: The Glass Has a Job Rule
rules.body: Use blur where an interface surface overlays the map or groups controls. Keep report text and evidence crisp.

rules.name: The Scan Before Style Rule
rules.body: Report titles and status lead; community and timing metadata follow in a quieter voice.

rules.name: The Readable Layer Rule
rules.body: The more text a surface carries, the more opaque its background becomes.

dos: Do keep the map as the first view and Community as a separate second view.
Do use glass for controls that float over map geography.
Do pair status color with a readable status label.
Do keep demo and sample disclosures visible in report content.
Do preserve keyboard focus, reduced-motion support, and comfortable touch targets.
donts: Don't place the full report feed over the map by default.
Don't blur report titles, source details, or evidence.
Don't use status color as the only signal of a report's state.
Don't style sample data as a verified live civic record.
